topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I kept circling back to our first day at the park, you know, the one where we shaped mud pies and laughed until the sun dipped below the playground. I couldn't help but trace the lines of those memories, how vivid they were, down to the way the light caught the swings. When I mentioned it today, the look on your face, it was like watching the sky cloud over without a whisper of wind. You spoke softly, as if the words were fragile, saying you didn't remember. I found myself pausing, mid-sentence, as if the breath had been caught somewhere between that old playground and this moment. It's as though the years we played out loud were now just my silent echoes.
